CZ Urges 1Password Users to Change All Passwords After Security Breach

1Password, a leading password management provider, disclosed a security breach in which attackers compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, injected malicious code into backend systems and stole customer information, including names, email addresses, account identifiers and certain invitation and recovery tokens.

Attackers also accessed private source code and the company's CI/CD system. 1Password said customer vaults, passwords and encryption keys remained secure, with no evidence of account takeovers. Binance founder CZ nevertheless urged users to change all their passwords, calling it "a pain in the neck, but necessary."

tweet.text:
Some thoughts on AI and finance. Equity investors tend to look at narratives and promises of new markets, so continued model performance gains are pretty critical to them. I think of the West Coast as a bit like this. Equity has unlimited upside and capped downside: worst case you lose x1 your investment.

Credit markets care about sustainability and survival. So fancy model demos don't matter, and they mostly look at whether token-serving supply outruns real demand. This is the East Coast. Credit is all about risk: if you lend $1bn to build a data center at 10% interest, and the borrower goes on to invent AGl and become worth $10 trillion, you still only get your 10% back.

I think the latter is at least part of the story for why the claimed Riemann hypothesis solution hasn't moved ANT stock much. Solving an old pure math problem does not immediately widen Anthropic's operating margins; and since interest rates are high, shareholders act more like the credit side and care more about n

Dario Rejects Claim He Wants to “Surrender Human Free Will” to AI, Calls It “Absurd”
> Responding to an Axios report, Anthropic CEO says AI must be governed democratically and that handing power to AI is “a terrible idea.”
Source:
https://x.com/DarioAmodei/status/2125656399392690605

tweet.text:
No, I do not believe that we should “surrender human free will” to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do. I have written hundreds of pages of essays and a constant theme in them is the need for AI to be governed by legitimate democratic processes. For millennia (going all the way back to Greek and Roman philosophers), advocates of autocracy have claimed that it leads to better, faster, or more decisive decision-making than the messy process of democracy. Even if this were true (which I doubt!), we should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.

No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different. For example in an interview on CBS a couple months ago, I specifically called for AI to be governed democratical

tweet.text:
Russia’s Largest Stock Exchange, Moscow Exchange (MOEX), to Launch Crypto Trading on December 1

According to Bits media, Moscow Exchange (MOEX) is set to launch crypto trading on December 1 (offering BTC, ETH, and USDT with an annual limit of 300,000 rubles per intermediary), but briefly announced on November 24 that December USDT trades would incur an extra 22% value-added tax (VAT) before deleting the notice hours later. Russia’s National Clearing Center explained that while issuerless BTC and ETH qualify as VAT-exempt "digital currencies," Tether-issued USDT is classified as a "foreign digital instrument" lacking VAT exemption—exposing corporate entities to an additional 25% profit tax on gains—as Tax Code amendments to waive the VAT have so far passed only their first reading.
